title: He works at OpenAI. Here's his advice for landing a job there.
excerpt: OpenAI product manager Ty Geri told Business Insider that the AI lab hires people who are passionate about the mission and experiment.
content_html:
He joined OpenAI. Here’s his advice for those who want a job at the lab.

By Henry Chandonnet

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

OpenAI job seekers, listen up.

Ty Geri joined the AI lab in 2025 as a product manager. Business Insider asked for his advice on landing a job at OpenAI — and he said that enthusiasm was key.

"I think OpenAI tries to hire people who are really passionate, and care, and want to be a part of this mission," he said.

Geri's advice is agnostic of role, he said: engineer, researcher, product manager, data scientist, whatever.

His other advice was to use the company's products. That doesn't mean he expects all the products to work instantaneously. Some will be "a little rough today," he said, but OpenAI is looking for people who are willing to "push on the frontiers."

"Try to bring these products into your life, into your workflows," Geri advised.

In July, a former OpenAI intern shared his advice with Business Insider. He said: go broad, specialize, and build. Another OpenAI employee said he got his job thanks in part to a cold DM on LinkedIn.

Sundeep Teki, a career coach who helps place talent at AI companies, told Business Insider in June that OpenAI had one of the hardest technical interviews in the industry. So, study up. Also, the labs sometimes recruit people from their public profiles, so keep contributing to that GitHub.

As for Geri, he said that the messiness of experimentation was core to OpenAI's culture. The company expects "a lot of building in public," he said.

Staffers at the company want to see what you're building and try it out for themselves, Geri said. He described a fallacy of work: "You sit in a dark room, you come out three years later, and you're like: 'Voila, magic.'" That doesn't fly at OpenAI.

"It definitely stresses me out," he said, "but I think it's part of the fun."

Among OpenAI employees, Geri said that there was a willingness to try new things. If the product you put out is "not quite it yet," Geri said that others at the company will try again.

The culture of experimentation and "big swings," as Geri calls them, is also what makes OpenAI different from his prior job at Google.

"Larger companies in the space can sometimes be a little bit slower," he said.

content_html_zh:
他加入了 OpenAI。 这是他给那些想在实验室工作的人的建议。

作者：Henry Chandonnet 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

OpenAI 求职者，听着。

Ty Geri 于 2025 年加入 AI 实验室，担任产品经理。 《商业内幕》询问他关于在 OpenAI 找到工作的建议，他说热情是关键。

“我认为 OpenAI 试图聘请那些真正充满热情、关心并希望成为这一使命一部分的人，”他说。

杰里的建议与角色无关，他说：工程师、研究员、产品经理、数据科学家，等等。

他的另一个建议是使用该公司的产品。 这并不意味着他希望所有产品都能立即发挥作用。 他说，有些人“今天会有点粗糙”，但 OpenAI 正在寻找愿意“推动前沿”的人。

“尝试将这些产品带入您的生活、工作流程中，”杰里建议道。

7 月，一位前 OpenAI 实习生向 Business Insider 分享了他的建议。 他说：宽广、专精、建设。 另一位 OpenAI 员工表示，他得到这份工作的部分原因是 LinkedIn 上的一条冷漠的私信。

Sundeep Teki 是一位帮助 AI 公司安置人才的职业教练，他在 6 月份告诉 Business Insider，OpenAI 的技术面试是业内最难的之一。 所以，好好学习吧。 此外，实验室有时会从他们的公开资料中招募人员，因此请继续为 GitHub 做出贡献。

至于 Geri，他表示混乱的实验是 OpenAI 文化的核心。 他说，该公司预计“将有大量公共建筑”。

杰里说，公司的员工想看看你正在建造什么，并亲自尝试一下。 他描述了一个工作谬误：“你坐在一个黑暗的房间里，三年后你出来，你会说：‘瞧，魔法。’”这在 OpenAI 是行不通的。

“这确实让我压力很大，”他说，“但我认为这是乐趣的一部分。”

Geri 表示，OpenAI 的员工愿意尝试新事物。 杰里说，如果你推出的产品“还不够完善”，公司的其他人会再试一次。

实验文化和杰里所说的“大转变”也是 OpenAI 与他之前在谷歌工作的不同之处。

“该领域的大公司有时可能会慢一些，”他说。
